title: wayfare map contract
description: Every value that has to be identical on both sides of the Python/JavaScript boundary. `publish` and `coverage.draw` read this file directly; the viewer reads `web/palette.js`, generated from it by `scripts/palette_js.py`. Nothing reports a mismatch at run time, which is why the shape is checked here.

colour.description: An sRGB colour as `#rrggbb`, lower case. Lower case is not a style rule: a mode's seed is the top step of its own ramp, the ramp is generated through OKLab and comes back lower case, and an upper-case seed would no longer equal the colour the legend draws for it.

ramp.description: Six steps, quietest first. Six because the legend draws one bar for the road ramp and every mode ramp together, and the ticks under it have to line up.

layer_name.description: A tippecanoe source-layer name. MapLibre tolerates a layer it names and the archive does not carry, drawing nothing and saying nothing.

attribute.description: A feature attribute name as written into the tiles.

mode_key.description: A mode name. Also a key on a generated JavaScript object, so it stays a plain identifier.

low.description: Where a mode ramp starts, relative to the mode's own colour: lightness is `min(cap, L * mul + add)` and chroma is `C * chroma`, both in OKLCh and both then fitted to sRGB. Two shapes of rule rather than one because light adds and clamps while dark multiplies.

layers.description: The three layer names inside an archive. tippecanoe writes them and MapLibre asks for them by name.

at.description: Journeys a day at each of the six steps, ascending. Interpolated in log10 between them, because journeys a day span three orders of magnitude and drawn straight everything but a handful of city corridors sits in the first colour. Must be strictly ascending, which JSON Schema cannot say and `palette.load` checks.

trips_per.description: `trips` on a tile feature is a count over this many days. The division to journeys a day happens where a ramp is evaluated and nowhere else.

needs.description: The attribute both ramps read. Published at every zoom: an attribute a paint property cannot find is not an error MapLibre reports, it takes the fallback and draws a whole country in the first ramp colour.

modes.description: One entry per non-road mode, in the order the legend lists them. `other` is required: it is what a mode this palette has never heard of is drawn as, which is what an archive built by a newer pipeline looks like to an older page.

label.description: What the legend calls this mode.

default_mode.description: What a track feature is drawn as where the tile carries no `mode`. Must be a key of [modes], which `palette.load` checks.

default.description: What `publish` writes when told neither a path nor to name the file for its region, and what both pages fall back to when there is no index to ask.

bands.description: Which band a feature came from, which is the only thing telling the two feature-id spaces apart: the detail band's id is the OpenStreetMap way id and the overview bands' is the Valhalla edge id.

detail_only.description: Attributes `publish` strips from the three overview bands.

sentinel.description: Whichever of `detail_only` the viewer tests the presence of. Must be in that list, which `palette.load` refuses to read a file without: a sentinel every band carries marks every feature as detail-band.

roam.description: The box a viewer will not pan outside of, and the one `art` warns a hand-written window against. Not the box that decides whether a stop is in these islands: that one is a capped line through the Channel rather than a rectangle, and lives in `config`.
